_comment: The user's OWN linker maps, and what each one holds. `mapsweep --manifest this
--root <where those repositories live>` reads them where they live and goes RED
when reality and this file part company, in EITHER direction.
THE PATHS ARE RELATIVE AND NAME A REPOSITORY, never an absolute location: a
tracked file carrying a username and a home-directory layout is a file that means
nothing on the next machine and goes stale the first time a directory moves.
THIS MATERIAL IS NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY and is not versioned here -- it is the
author's own, and one of the projects is unpublished. That is exactly why the
sweep is declared MANUAL in tests/gates-manual.txt: on the commit path it would be
INVALID in every clone but one.
THE NUMBERS WERE READ BY THE SHIPPED READER and then LOOKED AT. The
sweep can only tell you a count MOVED; whether a count is CORRECT is a judgement
made once, by a person, exactly as blessing any golden is.
_lineup_note: LineUp is EXPECTED to be refused, and that is a fact about how that project LINKS
rather than about this reader: its map is 42 lines of segment table with no
`Publics by ...` section at all, so there is no symbol in it to place. It has its
own card in that project's board. The expectation is the REASON and not merely
the fact of refusing -- every refusal is a refusal, so matching on 'it failed'
would accept a file that started failing for something else entirely.
_rechip_note: ReChip's is not a linker map at all: `make symbols` runs DJGPP's `nm` over the DEV
binary. It is in the sweep because it is one of the three projects this work exists
to cover, and because it is the only entry whose count moves whenever that program
does -- so a disagreement here is expected after real work there and is re-blessed
deliberately, which is the opposite of the finished programs above, whose maps
describe work that is not moving.
_format_coverage_note: THE FOUR ROWS BELOW EXIST BECAUSE THE SEVEN ABOVE ARE SIX BORLAND MAPS AND ONE
`nm` LISTING. This file's own reason for existing is that a format is not
demonstrated by one artefact, and it was demonstrating one format six times
while the two newest readers -- Open Watcom, and the SECTIONED Borland path --
had no real material here at all.
HELLO32 is the map that refuted the shipped reader in two measured ways (the
mark is `Idle` and not `idle`; the `Start` column is `section:offset` with every
offset zero). Its row pins what the corrected reader makes of it, so a relapse
on either point moves a number here.
THE TWO WATCOM MAPS ARE ONE SOURCE THROUGH LINKERS 32 YEARS APART, which is
what makes the pair worth more than either alone: they must both read, and
their counts differ (69 against 65) because the 1994 library is not the 2026
one. A reader that started ignoring the older one would still be green on the
newer.
THE GNU `ld` MAP IS NOT HERE AND THAT IS CORRECT: the only one is the fixture
this package generated, which lives INSIDE the repository, and the sweep exists
for material that does not. It is read by tests/test_dosbox_x_fixtures.py, where
its 912 non-symbol lines are pinned -- the number that keeps the majority-loss
refusal from ever being extended to the flat readers, where it would refuse every
GNU map ever written. A row for it here was written and then REFUSED by this
file's own relative-path guard, which is the guard working.
